extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers interested in wartime/current events
extracted.subtask_description: News reporting of wartime events (air raids, military operations, diplomatic visits) that supplies datelines, official statements, eyewitness accounts, and human-interest details to inform a general public. Emphasizes attribution, chronology, geographic specificity, and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline and source labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Use clear datelines and wire-service attribution (e.g., 'BERLIN, Sept. 18 (A. P.)', 'By the Associated Press', 'CAIRO, Sept. 18 (A. P.)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page repeatedly begins sections with location and date, followed by the news agency or byline. Examples: 'BERLIN, Sept. 18 (A. P.)', 'By the Associated Press', 'LONDON, Sept. 18 (A. P.).' This signals where and when reports originate and which service provided them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution to official communiques and spokesmen
rubrics_metrics.description: Attribute factual claims to specific official sources: 'the High Command reported', 'an authoritative spokesman said', 'the Italian High Command reported'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article attributes military claims and statistics to official communiques and spokesmen rather than presenting them as unverified facts. Examples include many references to 'the High Command' and 'authoritative spokesman'—use such attribution to indicate source and possible bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of eyewitness and participant quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate quotations from eyewitnesses, pilots, and participants (e.g., 'The pilot was quoted as saying', 'The pilot... said
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotation of eyewitness descriptions (the Nazi pilot describing London as 'a vast hot glowing spot') provides vivid detail and lends immediacy. Use direct quotes where available and attribute them clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precise chronology and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide precise times and sequences of events (e.g., lists of raid times: 'First daylight raid.............. 7.12 to 7.32 A.M.', 'Seventh daylight raid..... 5.10 to 5.54 P.M.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece lists exact raid windows and sequences to show tempo and progression. When reporting military operations, include chronological markers and exact times to clarify sequence and scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: Name specific locations and geographic features (cities, docks, airfields, roads): 'London', 'Tilbury', 'Sidi Barrani', 'Suez Canal', 'Alexandria', 'Bengazi', 'Derna'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article grounds events in named places (coastal roads, towns, ports). Precise place names help readers understand strategic significance and local impact; include them where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concrete casualty, damage, and material detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Report concrete outcomes and physical evidence (ships sunk, oil tanks burning, craters in subway, 'a 5,000-ton British ship... heavily damaged').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reporting enumerates burned warehouses, sunk ships, tonnage, and visible fires—use such tangible details to substantiate claims about impact and scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative data and operational figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Include numbers for losses, troop strengths, tonnage, planes shot down, and allocations (e.g., 'The Royal British Air Force has lost 621 planes...'; 'about 45,000 men are reported encamped').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing figures (even when sourced to official communiques) gives readers a sense of scale; always attribute numeric claims and note uncertainty when appropriate ('reported', 'claimed').

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance by presenting multiple perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Present claims from opposing sides and neutral/third-party observations (Axis press claims, British reports, neutral agency dispatches and observers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article juxtaposes German press/pilot accounts, Italian communiques, and British statements/analysis. To avoid one-sidedness, present differing accounts and label their provenance so readers can weigh credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human-interest and anecdotal elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Include human stories and dramatic anecdotes to illustrate impact (rescue of victims, ambulance driver accounts, 'a baby and five women' rescued).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The narrative intersperses operational reporting with personal rescue scenes and localized consequences. Such vignettes humanize the conflict and help readers connect emotionally; use sparingly and respectfully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert or correspondent analysis and strategic context
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide analysis of strategic intent and likely consequences (e.g., objectives of raids: 'Disorganization of London’s communications' and 'Demoralization of the civilian population'; discussion of Ribbentrop’s visit and Axis coordination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond raw facts, the piece offers interpretation from observers and officials about goals and implications. Include expert/correspondent analysis to situate events within broader geopolitical strategy, clearly marking it as analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mention of secrecy, censorship, and official restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Note government secrecy or restricted sessions where relevant (e.g., 'The House went into a secret session... debate took place on the recent aerial bombardment').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article flags when information is limited by secrecy or official restraints. When reporting under such conditions, acknowledge limits to verifyability and possible constraints on available information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connection to wider political/economic measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Link military events to diplomatic and economic actions (e.g., blockade application talks, oil pacts, Ribbentrop's visit to Rome, Swiss mission discussing ship releases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reporting connects front-line events to diplomacy and economics (blockades, trade, ship seizures). Including this context helps readers understand secondary effects and policy responses.
